predictions.title: OECD GENAI cyber-eval reciprocity attestation Recommendation lands by Q3 2026
predictions.body: By Q3 2026 the Thursday OECD GENAI working-group secretariat procedural note — formalizing the Indo-Pacific cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation field schema as a draft Recommendation text for member-state circulation in the June 2-6 plenary window — combined with the Thursday cross-continental cohort expansion (the United Arab Emirates Cybersecurity Council and the Israel National Cyber Directorate jointly publishing the first Middle East formal exploratory-observer commitment, Saudi Arabia National Cybersecurity Authority's adjacent-track pre-commitment marking the first GCC adjacent extension, and the cohort's named-candidate count crossing to thirteen formal-plus-observer-plus-exploratory jurisdictions plus the originating UK and EU) and the Thursday Mistral Workflows public-preview shipment of a formal cyber-eval reciprocity attestation matrix supporting all thirteen-jurisdiction tenant-policy field schemas as the first cross-vendor matrix-tier interop deliverable, forces the OECD GENAI working-group to adopt the attestation field schema as a formal OECD Recommendation rather than holding it as a sub-working-group technical note. The trigger is the simultaneous Thursday landing of three structurally complementary moves: the secretariat's procedural note publishes a citable draft Recommendation text with explicit June 2-6 plenary member-state circulation calendar (moving the schema from informal sub-working-group artifact to OECD Recommendation candidate); the cross-continental cohort gains its first Middle East formal entry (UAE) plus its first GCC adjacent track (Saudi Arabia) plus its first jointly-co-published Middle East entry (UAE + Israel) on the same Thursday wire, demonstrating that the perimeter no longer reads as Indo-Pacific-only and pre-empts the most plausible plenary objection that the schema reflects only one regional bloc's interests; and the Mistral Workflows public-preview cross-orchestrator interop matrix ships supporting all thirteen-jurisdiction tenant-policy field schemas as a private-sector lived demonstration that the schema is already an operative multi-vendor procurement primitive ahead of any OECD action. The structural force is procedural rather than political: when the secretariat itself publishes a draft Recommendation text with a named plenary circulation window AND the cohort has already crossed regional-bloc boundaries AND a major private-sector cross-orchestrator interop matrix ships matrix-tier support for the field schemas, the OECD member-state adoption pathway compresses correspondingly because the Recommendation text now functions as a procedural floor — declining adoption would require an affirmative reason from each member-state given the schema's existing multi-vendor uptake. The landing shape: by Q3 2026 the OECD Council adopts the cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation field schema as a formal OECD Recommendation, at least one additional OECD member-state outside the existing Indo-Pacific cohort (likely Mexico, Chile, Colombia, or Costa Rica from the Latin American track, or one of the Continental European allied-defense industrial-base jurisdictions newly anchored by the Anthropic Thursday Continental defense gating extension) joins the perimeter under the Recommendation umbrella, and at least one hyperscaler agent-registry GA tier cites the OECD Recommendation rather than the underlying bilateral memoranda as the operative tenant-policy schema reference. Bear case is the June 2-6 plenary defers the draft Recommendation text to a fall session pending the FMRB executive order signing posture (so that the OECD Recommendation can be coordinated with a US reciprocity-mirror clause); absent that deferral, Q3 2026 lands the OECD Recommendation as the operative multilateral umbrella for the cyber-eval reciprocity attestation field schema, formally lifting the schema above the Indo-Pacific bilateral-memoranda baseline.

reasoning.because: Thursday OECD secretariat publishes draft Recommendation text for June 2-6 plenary circulation.
reasoning.given: Cohort crosses to 13 jurisdictions with first Middle East and GCC adjacent entries Thursday.
reasoning.so_that: OECD Council adopts the attestation field schema as a formal Recommendation.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; OECD Recommendation plus one new member-state entry.
reasoning.plain_language: An international group is drafting an official rule that requires AI tools to pass safety checks shared between countries.

predictions.summary: Thursday's OECD GENAI secretariat note formalizes the cyber-eval reciprocity attestation field schema as a draft Recommendation for the June 2-6 plenary, paired with the cohort's first Middle East and GCC extensions plus Mistral's matrix-tier interop shipment. By Q3 2026 the OECD Council adopts it.
